title: BIPAP- versus flow-controlled ventilation in burn patients: A monocentric, randomised controlled trial
summary:
In the intensive care unit setting patients are often in need of controlled ventilation. Also burn patients can be in need of controlled ventilation for an effective pain therapy and/or if their lungs are severely injured. Mechanical ventilation itself can induce an injury in the lungs. Up to now, intensive care patients are very often pressure-controlled ventilated in Germany.

Flow-controlled ventilation is a new mode for controlled ventilation. Airway flows are low and smooth during inspiration and expiration - as a sharp contrast to conventional modes. This new mode might stress the lungs less than conventional pressure-controlled ventilation.

With this study we want to show that the mechanical power during inspiration of burn patients is reduced when flow-controlled ventilation is applied compared to pressure-controlled ventilation.

In total 24 burn patients in need of ventilation will be ventilated either with  flow- or pressure-controlled ventilation for up to 70 hours. Patients will be randomly assigned to one group with an allocation ratio of 1:1.
During controlled ventilation mechnical power is computed according to certain ventilatory parameters. Additionally, we evaluate organ functions of the cardiovascular systems, the lungs and other organs during and after the group-specific ventilation.

Patients can participate in this study, if
- they are adult but not older than 80 years
- they are either not mechanically ventilated or ventilated for less than 24 hours before admission to the Burn Centre
- they need (further) controlled ventilation for at least 24 hours .
conditions: Burn patients in need of ventilation

interventions.name: Flow-controlled ventilation (FCV) with an individualised positive end-expiratory pressure and an individualised driving pressure, resulting in a liberal tidal volume
Controlled Biphasic Positive Airway Pressure (BIPAP) ventilation with an individualised positive end-expiratory pressure and a driving pressure  for a tidal volume of 6-8 ml/kg predicted body weight

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- in already ventilated patients: invasive ventilation for ≤ 24 hours before admission to the Burn Centre
- in not ventilated patients: indication for tracheal intubation and controlled ventilation within 48 hours of admission to the Burn Centre
- estimated (further) duration of ventilation ≥ 24 hours
- start of intervention ≤ 48 hours after admission to the Burn Centre
- a central venous catheter and an arterial line for the intensive care treatment
- signed informed consent by the patient or a legal presentative, by a representative of the patients will in incompetent patients or by a study-independent physician in charge in incompetent patients without a respresentative of the patients will
Exclusion criteria:
- participation in another interventional trial
- invasive ventilation for > 24 hours before admission to the Burn Centre
- start of the intervention > 48 hours after admission to the Burn Centre
- estimated (further) duration of ventilation < 24 hours
- no informed consent by the patient, by a legal representative, by a representative of the patients will in incompetent patients or by a study-independent physician in charge in incompetent patients without a respresentative of the patients will
